deficiencies.description: The rewrite states that the cervix is seen 'alongside' the endocervical canal, converting the lecturer's pointing gesture ('and so you're looking at the cervix here') into an unsourced spatial description. Because the endocervical canal is the passage through the cervix, describing the cervix as being alongside the canal is anatomically inaccurate and may lead students to view them as separate adjacent structures.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: Histologically, this is the endocervical canal here, and so you're looking at the cervix here.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: Histologically, the endocervical canal runs through the neck of the womb, and the cervix is seen alongside it.

considerations.reason: This is a remark directing the audience's attention to specific individual cells on a slide image; the core teaching point that mitotic cells occur at the basement membrane is preserved.
